purpose: Make mature OSS adoption analysis a mandatory pre-implementation and pre-RED-repair step. Yance must adopt or port mature upstream products, sidecars, source modules, official SDKs, native prebuilds, packaging/runtime tools, or existing mature repository seams before authorizing equivalent self-built infrastructure.
decisionRules: Before any new work package or implementation, identify who already owns the capability in mature OSS or in an already-adopted repository seam.
Before fixing any causal RED, repeat OSS-fit for the failing layer instead of assuming the existing Yance wrapper should be repaired.
If a mature OSS full product can own the capability, prefer adopting it over rebuilding an equivalent Yance subsystem.

If a full product is not appropriate, evaluate mature sidecar/service, upstream source-module port, official SDK/CLI/native-prebuild/runtime, and existing repository seam in that order before Yance implementation.
When mature OSS can replace an existing equivalent Yance self-built path, authorization must identify the path to retire or explicitly prohibit parallel duplicate authority.
Reading or copying upstream design and then rewriting an equivalent Yance engine is not OSS adoption.
A minimal Yance gap is admissible only after the authorization records the uncovered capability and why the preceding adoption modes cannot satisfy it.
CI, UAT, runtime, packaging, downloader, cache, materializer, installer, package-manager, and native-build fixes are subject to the same OSS-first rule as product features.
